features.title: Browser-like tabs above the main view
features.summary: Every thread or global panel shown in the main view opens or focuses a tab above it. The strip looks like DSH's own right-panel tabs (28px pills, hairline separators, a close cross over a faded title end). Tabs close with × or a middle click, reorder by drag, pin to the start, close others or to the right from their context menu, scroll or list in a dropdown when they overflow, and show working, needs-you and unread dots on thread tabs. A thread tab's menu opens that thread in the right side panel — through the cancelable `dshfiles:open-thread-aside` event `@dshfiles/thread-sidebar` answers, with the strip saying the panel is unavailable when no plugin takes it — and dragging a thread tab onto the open side panel moves it there instead: the right column highlights under the pointer, and dropping closes the main tab once the aside took the thread. The aside tab's own menu moves it back through `dshfiles:open-thread`. Thread tabs also copy their ID or a clean deep link. Opening from outside the strip uses a VS Code-style preview tab by default; double-clicking a sidebar thread keeps its tab open.

configuration.constraints: Boolean; show the tab strip and follow the main view.
Integer 2–50; past it the least recently used unpinned tab closes.
What opening from outside the strip does: preview tab, new tab, or replace the current tab.

failureModes: A tab whose panel plugin is gone stays dimmed until the panel registers again; picking it does nothing.
A navigation the Host never finishes stops being awaited after two seconds.
Tabs of deleted threads are dropped.

Open in side panel leaves the thread alone and the strip announces that the side panel is unavailable there when no plugin offers an aside, and a request with no thread on screen is declined the same way.

Dragging a panel tab over the right column asks its plugin through the cancelable `dshfiles:move-panel-aside` event. A panel whose plugin offers no side-panel view keeps its tab and the strip says so; a panel tab is only moved when its owner cancels the request.
A thread dropped where the aside owner declined the request keeps its main tab and announces the unavailable side panel; dragging where the right sidebar is not mounted highlights nothing.

If DSH stops rendering the main slot outlet (`[data-slot="main"]`) the strip stays hidden, tabs keep following the main view, and the console warns once at startup; if the strip lands anywhere but directly above the main panel, the console warns too.

features.title: Open a new tab with suggestions of what to show
features.summary: "+" at the end of the strip (or Mod+T on Desktop, Mod+Alt+T on the Web) opens a compact Start tab: New thread and the five most recent threads (running ones first) sit beside the main panels and Settings when the pane is wide, and stack in one column when narrow. Arrow keys, Home/End and Enter work in the list; the picked thread or panel takes the Start tab's place, while New thread and Settings close it.
failureModes: The Start page is never saved: a reload drops it.
A panel glyph that throws outside the sidebar falls back to a generic panel icon.
Settings opens by pressing the sidebar's own Settings trigger; without that trigger the Settings suggestion only closes the Start tab.
Opening, from the sidebar, the very view the Host already shows under the Start page leaves the Start page in front: the Host reports no change.

features.title: Jump between tabs from the keyboard
features.summary: Desktop Mod+W closes the active tab without archiving its thread; with no active tab the normal window-close action remains. Mod+1…8 jump to a tab and Mod+9 to the last one, Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab cycle (Desktop); the browser keeps those keys, so the Web defaults are Mod+Alt+1…9 and Mod+Alt+] / [. All are rebindable in Settings › Shortcuts. Arrow keys, Enter and Delete work inside the focused strip. Mod+T (Web: Mod+Alt+T) opens a new tab.
failureModes: A default another command already owns leaves that tab command listed but unbound.

features.title: Keep tabs across reloads, per project or globally
features.summary: The tab set, order, pins, preview flag and active tab survive a reload; each project keeps its own set unless the persistence setting shares one set across projects. A reload that lands on the New thread screen reopens the saved active tab.

configuration.constraints: project keeps a tab set per project (jj thread workspaces count as their project); global shares one.

failureModes: A malformed saved document is ignored and tabs start empty.
